sections.title: Form and leaves
sections.text: This large solitary palm, native to the southern Caribbean and northern South America, reaches about 18–40 m tall and 46–66 cm in stem diameter. Its grey stem carries a crown of large pinnate leaves, often held almost horizontally.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Branched inflorescences emerge below the green crownshaft. They bear small pale flowers followed by blue-violet, ovoid fruits at maturity. The plate matches the species’ tall form, pinnate fronds and fruit.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Horticultural and ethnobotanical sources report that the terminal bud, or palm heart, is eaten as a vegetable. Harvesting it kills the palm. This does not establish that the fruits, seeds or other parts are edible.
